title: Asian Games Cricket Champions Return Home After Defending Gold Against Pakistan
excerpt: India's men landed in Delhi and Hyderabad to a warm welcome a day after head coach VVS Laxman hailed the 19-run win over Pakistan as a matter of great pride for Indian cricket.
body:
• India beat Pakistan by 19 runs in the men's T20 final at Korogi Sports Park, Nisshin, on October 3 — defending the gold first won at Hangzhou 2023.
  • Head coach VVS Laxman said winning gold at the Asian Games "is a matter of great pride," praising the squad's champion's mindset after it held its nerve under pressure.
  • Players including Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson and Arshdeep Singh were photographed arriving at Delhi's IGI Airport; Tilak Varma landed in Hyderabad to fan greetings.
  • India finished the Games with 85 medals (21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze), below its record haul of 106 at Hangzhou.

New Delhi: India's Asian Games cricket champions are home. A day after beating Pakistan by 19 runs to defend the men's T20 gold at Nisshin, Japan, members of the squad touched down in Delhi and Hyderabad on Sunday to fan greetings and a fresh round of tributes led by head coach VVS Laxman.

Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson and Arshdeep Singh were photographed at Delhi's Indira Gandhi International Airport, while Tilak Varma — one of the final's standout performers — arrived at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad, where supporters had gathered to welcome him.

Laxman's verdict

Laxman, who served as India's head coach for the Asian Games men's squad, was effusive about the achievement. "Very pleased with the way the team played; getting a gold in the Asian Games is a matter of great pride," he told reporters, according to ANI. "Defending the [title] is also a very special moment."

He praised the squad's composure through a weather-disrupted tournament — rain followed the team from Tokyo to the Nisshin venue. "We are very lucky to have so many players who are so talented, hard-working, and have a great work ethic, and also, most importantly, who have got a champion's mindset," Laxman said. "Even though they were challenged by the weather or the conditions, they stepped up. And especially when they were under pressure, I thought they held their nerve and got the desired result for the country."

"Very pleased with the way the team played; getting a gold in the Asian Games is a matter of great pride."

— VVS Laxman, head coach, India men's team

Speaking after the final on Saturday, Laxman had noted the personal significance for a squad stacked with World Cup winners. "Two years back, we won in China, and again now… A lot of them have won the World Cup, but for many of them, this is the first time they're winning the gold medal," he said. "I'm sure it's a matter of great pride for all of them."

The final, in brief

India posted 211 for 6 in 20 overs, powered by Abhishek Sharma's 61 off 28 balls — the fastest fifty by an Indian against Pakistan in T20Is, off just 20 deliveries — and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 off 22. A 62-run sixth-wicket stand between Varma and Shivam Dube (27 not out) pushed India past 200. Pakistan's chase stalled on 192 for 6, despite Hasan Nawaz's 96 off 51; Dube dismissed him off the final ball. Washington Sundar, Axar Patel and Dube took two wickets each.

The final carried the now-familiar edge of recent India-Pakistan contests: the two captains did not shake hands at the toss.

The bigger picture

The victory completed a back-to-back gold run. At Hangzhou 2023, India took the title when the final against Afghanistan was washed out and the medal awarded on higher ranking; this time the team won it on the field. India's women also struck gold, beating Sri Lanka in their final.

The cricket gold was part of an 85-medal haul that placed India fourth in the overall table — short of the record 106 medals (28 gold) at Hangzhou, but a strong showing for a contingent that included several breakthrough performances across athletics, boxing, archery and hockey.

What next

For most of the squad, the Asian Games was a mid-season assignment between international commitments; the players now rejoin their teams ahead of a packed calendar. The more lasting question is whether cricket's Asian Games presence — in a T20 format that fits the multi-sport template — builds momentum toward the sport's Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028, where India will arrive as back-to-back Asian champions.
